originality.rationale: The complete all-64 length-six universal-prime cutoff and sharp 457 obstruction were not found in inspected primary claims, mathematical searches, indexed research records. Wang/Fang address lengths up to five and homogeneous progressions; Keith Conrad supplies the general Weil-bound counting method but not the exact cutoff; Buchaev/Tsfasman 2026 covers arbitrary patterns only of lengths four and five by its abstract. Related homogeneous length-six formulas do not individually establish the full mixed-word threshold; a residual unindexed-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: The full text (including potential tables or appendices) of Buchaev–Tsfasman arXiv:2607.17418 was inaccessible; assessed only its explicit length-four/five abstract.

The assessed prior mathematical statements did not contain the same six-letter cutoff.

value.rationale: The least universal prime for simultaneous presence of every six-letter Legendre sign word is a natural arithmetic-complexity invariant. The exact sharp cutoff 461, with immediately preceding last obstruction 457, moves beyond recent length-four/five mixed-sign character-pattern classifications. Proof gives both finite sharpness and an unbounded analytic tail; it is not an arbitrary isolated congruence or restatement of the Weil bound.
